title: Yara and the Ember
premise: Wendell Brightwater, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden her magic for seven years in Grayhollow, a city where spellcraft is punishable by burning. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, she learns that Yara—a foundling girl she raised as a daughter—was sold at birth to the court beneath the mountain, and the falling stars are the price of that contract coming due. Wendell must gather a crew of outlaws, exiles, and one repentant inquisitor to descend into the Ember Court and steal Yara's soul back before the last star gutters out. In the end, Wendell breaks her own oath to save Yara, discovering that loyalty kept in silence was never loyalty at all—and that truth, spoken aloud even at ruinous cost, is the only magic the law cannot outlaw.
about_author: Cyrus Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who break rules for love, from a house full of cats and questionable candles.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In Grayhollow's night market, Wendell sells harmless charms while hiding her swordspeaker oaths beneath a merchant's smile. She dreads the anniversary of the Purge. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of invisibility, and the warmth of her small found family around Yara.

chapters.title: A Girl Made of Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Yara turns sixteen; Wendell gives her a locket charmed against forgetting. Yara asks, again, where she came from. Wendell deflects. Emotional beat: tenderness laced with guilt—the lie Wendell tells herself is protection.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The sky goes black star by star; the border wards shatter like glass. Panic floods Grayhollow, and the Inquisition immediately blames unregistered mages. Emotional beat: dread—the world Wendell hid from just arrived at her door.

chapters.title: What the Locket Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The locket hums and shows Yara fragments: a mountain gate, a voice like coals, a signature on a contract. She realizes Wendell knows more than she's said. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sting, and stubborn curiosity.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor at the Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Inquisitor Serah Vane—sharp, weary, once Wendell's friend before the Purge—comes searching for illegal charms. Wendell lies badly. Serah leaves a warning instead of irons. Emotional beat: old loyalty stretched over new law.

chapters.title: Sold Before She Could Speak
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, flashback-heavy. Wendell confesses to herself what she's buried: Yara's dying mother sold the child's soul to the Ember Court to buy passage through the wards. Emotional beat: shame crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Running Toward the Mountain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara flees toward the mountain alone, following the locket's pull, convinced she's saving Wendell from exposure. Emotional beat: fierce, misguided independence.

chapters.title: The Crew Nobody Wants
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell recruits help: Brannoc, a disgraced ward-smith; Pip, a thief who can hear locks; and Marisol, an exile hedge-witch with a grudge against the Inquisition. Emotional beat: reluctant hope—found family assembling itself.

chapters.title: Serah's Ledger
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah discovers the Inquisition knew the stars' disappearance was contractual, not criminal—and that her superiors helped broker it. Emotional beat: faith cracking against institutional rot.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash Bells
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The crew travels the dead borderlands, passing villages emptied by fear. Brannoc teaches Wendell how the wards were truly built—with souls as mortar. Emotional beat: grief widening into anger.

chapters.title: Caught Between Laws
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah intercepts the crew but lets them go, demanding truth in exchange. Wendell gives it—all of it, including Yara's contract. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—truth offered freely buys what force never could.

chapters.title: Locks That Sing
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip breaks the crew into a waystation vault holding Ember Court correspondence. They learn the final star dies in nineteen days, and with it, Yara. Emotional beat: ticking-clock terror, gallows humor as armor.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reaches the mountain gate and is welcomed—too warmly—by the Ember Court's herald, who calls her 'the payment.' Emotional beat: seductive belonging masking captivity.

chapters.title: Oath and Iron
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell attempts to speak her swordspeaker oath aloud for the first time in seven years and finds it rusted shut—oaths decay when abandoned. Emotional beat: despair; the past won't arm her after all.

chapters.title: Nineteen Candles
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reads the court's candle-magic: each extinguished star is a soul already collected. Yara will be the last, completing the contract that keeps something beneath the mountain asleep—or fed. Emotional beat: horror reframing the stakes.

chapters.title: The Herald's Kindness
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The court treats Yara like royalty; she almost believes she belongs here more than in Grayhollow. Then she sees the nursery of other 'payments' who came before. Emotional beat: comfort curdling into clarity.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc reveals he helped build the wards and names the price he paid: his brother's soul, the first payment. He joins the descent not for redemption but for a body to bury. Emotional beat: guilt as fuel.

chapters.title: Descent Through the Wards' Bones
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The crew enters the mountain through the skeleton of the original ward-work, Pip singing locks open while the dark presses close. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and fragile trust.

chapters.title: The First Lie Told Aloud
chapters.summary: Wendell and Yara reunite in the antechamber. Yara demands the whole truth; Wendell gives it, kneeling. Yara doesn't forgive—not yet—but walks beside her. Emotional beat: rupture acknowledged, repair begun.

chapters.title: Court of Coals and Courtesy
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The crew infiltrates the Ember Court mid-audience, disguised as tribute-bearers. The Ember Queen speaks in Wendell's own dead master's voice. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; nothing here can be trusted at face value.

chapters.title: The Contract's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip steals the original contract and finds the loophole: the debt may be paid by any soul willingly given of equal weight—or dissolved if the seller's intent is proven fraudulent. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: A Mother's Intent
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah tracks down records proving Yara's mother was coerced by Inquisition agents into the sale—the same agents Serah once served. Emotional beat: complicity and the choice to testify anyway.

chapters.title: The Queen's Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Ember Queen offers Wendell a trade: Yara's freedom for Wendell's own soul, freely given—an oath finally worthy of her rusted voice. Emotional beat: temptation that isn't temptation at all; she'd say yes.

chapters.title: Refusal Is Also a Choice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara refuses to let Wendell pay, invoking the fraud clause before the assembled court with Serah's evidence. The court convulses; the Queen's mask slips. Emotional beat: Yara claiming agency—she is no one's payment.

chapters.title: When the Last Star Guttered
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The final star dies above the mountain. The contract executes early; the court begins collecting Yara by force. Battle erupts in the coal-lit hall. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, everything staked at once.

chapters.title: The Oath Remembered
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Watching Yara fight alone, Wendell understands: her oath was never to the order that fell—it was to protect. She speaks it anew, in her own words, and iron answers. Emotional beat: transcendence; the sword remembers its speaker.

chapters.title: Steel Against Ember
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Wendell duels the Ember Queen while Brannoc collapses the collection engine and Pip frees the stored souls. Emotional beat: fury and grace—every hidden year spent in a single fight.

chapters.title: The Weight of One Soul
chapters.summary: Climax turns. The Queen offers the true bargain: dissolve the contract, or the mountain opens and the thing beneath wakes hungry. Someone must stay to hold the seal. Emotional beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: What Marisol Carried
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals she has been carrying her own death-candle since exile—her soul was already forfeit. She takes the seal willingly, calling it settling accounts. Emotional beat: devastating, chosen sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Contract
chapters.summary: Climax resolves. With Marisol sealing the deep and the fraud clause ratified by the court's own law, the contract burns. Yara's soul returns to her body in a rush of light. Emotional beat: release—grief and joy in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Dark
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The crew carries Marisol's candle up the mountain. The stars do not return yet, but one faint point kindles—Marisol's. Emotional beat: mourning braided with wonder.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah testifies before Grayhollow's council, exposing the Inquisition's role in the sale. She is stripped of rank and chooses exile beside the people she hunted. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for personally.

chapters.title: The City That Outlawed Magic
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Grayhollow, seeing the returned star, begins questioning its own edicts. Wendell openly lights a charm in the market square and waits for the mob. It doesn't come. Emotional beat: trembling liberation.

chapters.title: Yara's Own Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara formally takes her mother's surname, reclaiming the lineage the contract tried to erase. She asks Wendell to teach her the swordspeak—not as legacy, but as inheritance chosen. Emotional beat: identity forged rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Letters to the Dead
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc buries his brother's recovered soul-candle under a rowan tree and finally weeps. Pip stands with him without a word. Emotional beat: grief given ritual and witness.

chapters.title: The Rebuilding of the Wards
chapters.summary: Wendell and Brannoc's POV. Together they design new border wards built on consent—each contributor volunteering a spark, not a soul. Emotional beat: collective repair; systems can be remade kinder.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Wendell and Yara's quiet chapter. Over Yara's seventeenth birthday, they speak plainly about the years of silence. Forgiveness arrives not as absolution but as agreement to keep choosing each other. Emotional beat: earned reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Second Star
chapters.summary: Ensemble. A second star ignites—then a third. The freed souls are finding their way home. The city watches the sky together for the first time without fear. Emotional beat: communal awe; the found family widens to include a city.

chapters.title: An Oath Renewed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell re-founds no order, writes no charter. Instead she takes one apprentice—Yara—and swears a single-sentence oath aloud in the market square. Emotional beat: humility; legacies are small and human.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating Wendell and Yara. On the mountain's slope, they visit Marisol's seal, which glows steady and warm. Below, Grayhollow's lights answer the returning stars. Emotional beat: peace hard-won—loyalty and truth no longer at war, but hand in hand.
